_comment: Exhaustive by policy: every writable field is declared, so nothing is
silently unmanaged. Server-generated fields (id, timestamps, urls,
counts, pushed_at) are excluded by the projection in project.jq — they
are not settable and would be permanent false drift.
allow_forking is true because GitHub forces it on public repositories.
are declared disabled because they cannot be enabled here. A PATCH to
enable either returns 200 and changes nothing — they need GitHub Advanced
Security, which a personal public repo does not have. Declaring 'enabled'
The AZURE_* and TFSTATE_* variables come from `terraform output
github_environment_variables` in terraform/bootstrap. They are identifiers,
not credentials: under OIDC the federated subject authorises, and it names
this repository and one environment. AZURE_CLIENT_ID is per-environment and
lives in environments.json instead, so `environment:` selects the identity.
prune_variables is true, so anything set by hand in the UI and not declared
here is deleted on the next reconcile. These four had to land before cd.yml
